Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

matchdb (development version)

The normalizer comes from npnormalize

  • matchdb now imports npnormalize for the normalizer and its signature, and only suggests npmatch. Every call to the 9 normalizer functions (np_normalize(), np_normalize_signature(), np_stopwords(), np_name_freq(), np_token_idf(), np_name_core(), np_name_rules(), np_name_placeholder(), np_addr_freq()) goes to npnormalize.
  • The signature is unchanged, v1-3e7b9f9d59bbb19e, so the published database, bundles and tranches are all still accepted. Nothing needs rebuilding.
  • npmatch is needed only to match, and for md_reference(build_index = TRUE), which builds npmatch’s blocking index. Without npmatch the index is skipped with a message; npmatch builds it itself when given none.
  • md_place_key(), md_unit_id() and md_addr_freq() call npnormalize directly: np_addr_key(), np_unit_id() and np_addr_freq().
    • Before, they looked for these functions in npmatch. With an npmatch that no longer holds the normalizer, they quietly fell back to matchdb’s own copies.
    • The copies are removed. They had agreed with npnormalize on every distinct value in the database.
    • matchdb now requires npnormalize 0.1.1, the first version to export np_unit_id().

Stamps and the workspace log record npnormalize

  • Compile stamps, bundle stamps, tranche manifests, source pins and source_vintage gain npnormalize_version beside npmatch_version, which is now NA when npmatch is not installed. Old stamps stay readable. A database built before this gains the source_vintage column the next time a source is recorded; its old rows keep NULL.
  • The workspace log records npnormalize_version and npnormalize_commit, and a change in either is a version_change row. An older logs/runs-index.csv is rewritten once, adding the two columns, the next time an action is logged.

matchdb 0.1.1

The first tagged release, v0.1.1. Its number matches npmatch 0.1.1, the release it pairs with: both are the last versions before the normalizer moves into the npnormalize package. Pin both, in renv or with @v0.1.1, for anything that should reproduce results from before that move.

Pairs with

  • npmatch 0.1.1 (npmatch (>= 0.1.1); Remotes: pins @v0.1.1).
  • Normalizer signature v1-3e7b9f9d59bbb19e. Everything published so far was built with this signature, and everything matchdb reads checks it: the database, the four tier bundles and the parquet tranches.

The published data at this release

Built on 2026-10-26 from main at 592b078 with npmatch 26a5910. It is all public at https://nccs-efile.s3.amazonaws.com/dev/matchdb; no AWS account is needed.

  • MATCHDB.duckdb (11.7 GB, 26 tables) is the user copy, fetched by md_fetch_db(). MATCHDB-full.duckdb (24.3 GB) adds the observation ledger, for maintainers.
  • Four tier bundles, read by md_reference(): active-legal (2.74M rows), active-observed (2.89M), unified-legal (4.98M) and unified-observed (5.13M).
  • Parquet tranches, build 2026-10-27-82c6f0cb (108 files, 4.64 GB). md_fetch_tranches(spec) downloads only the files a spec needs: about 1.0 GB for an active-layer spec.

What is in this release

  • Building the database:
    • the ingests for the BMF, NTEE, 1023-EZ, e-file headers, Schedule I, Schedule R, group exemptions, 527 filings, the 990-N e-Postcard, revocations, websites and officer name keys;
    • content-hash ids, and the append-only observation ledger with rollups (dev/IDENTITY.md);
    • the stored normalizer columns, compact tables, EIN keys, typed clusters, places, and the statistics cells.
  • Compiling: md_spec() and md_compile().
    • A spec chooses layers, name and address classes, sources and corroboration.
    • The compiled frame is checked against np_normalize() on every compile.
    • Compiling reports what the spec leaves out.
  • Publishing:
    • md_publish() writes signed bundles, and md_reference() refuses a stale or altered one;
    • md_publish_tranches() writes the database as parquet, split by layer and class.
  • Getting data:
    • md_fetch_reference(), md_fetch_db() and md_fetch_tranches(), over plain HTTPS, with md5 checks;
    • md_tranche_db(), a connection over the downloaded files that md_compile(), md_publish(), md_lookup() and md_cluster() take unchanged.
  • The workspace:
    • one folder, md_data_root();
    • the log: md_log() and md_log_run(), with logs/runs-index.csv append-only;
    • md_status(), the current state, kept in logs/state.json;
    • version_change rows, written when the data build, the npmatch version or the normalizer changes;
    • md_tranches(), md_tranche_manifest(), md_tranche_diff() and md_tranches_prune(), for seeing what is published and updating to a new build;
    • the guide, vignette("workspace").
  • Looking things up: md_lookup() and md_cluster().

Checks at this release

  • Phase 1 gate: three zeros against the frozen baseline.
  • Phase 2: +146 YES on the 1k benchmark.
  • check-build: 36 of 36.
  • Tranches: each tier compiled from its own tranches is identical to its bundle.
  • The logs are in dev/verify/logs/.
